title: Substitution with closed bodies
starter:
type term =
  | Num of int
  | Param of int
  | Add of term * term
  | Call of term * term list   (* Call (body, args) *)

(* Given: prints a term. Keep it; the tests use it. *)
let rec show = function
  | Num n -> string_of_int n
  | Param i -> "p" ^ string_of_int i
  | Add (a, b) -> "add(" ^ show a ^ ", " ^ show b ^ ")"
  | Call (f, args) -> "call(" ^ show f ^ ", [" ^ String.concat "; " (List.map show args) ^ "])"

(* Replace every Param i reachable from t with the i-th arg (leave it alone if there's no i-th arg).
   A nested Call's body is closed: don't go inside it. Its args are not closed: do. *)
let rec subst (args : term list) (t : term) : term =
  t
hints: Write one case per constructor. `Num` has nothing to replace. `Param i` is the only place a replacement happens.
For `Param i`, look up the i-th arg with `List.nth_opt` and keep the `Param` when there isn't one. `Add` just recurses into both sides.
For `Call (f, xs)`, recurse into the args `xs` but leave the body `f` exactly as it is. Its params belong to that inner call, not to you.

answer.code:
type term =
  | Num of int
  | Param of int
  | Add of term * term
  | Call of term * term list   (* Call (body, args) *)

(* Given: prints a term. Keep it; the tests use it. *)
let rec show = function
  | Num n -> string_of_int n
  | Param i -> "p" ^ string_of_int i
  | Add (a, b) -> "add(" ^ show a ^ ", " ^ show b ^ ")"
  | Call (f, args) -> "call(" ^ show f ^ ", [" ^ String.concat "; " (List.map show args) ^ "])"

let rec subst args t = match t with
  | Num _ -> t
  | Param i -> (match List.nth_opt args i with Some a -> a | None -> t)
  | Add (a, b) -> Add (subst args a, subst args b)
  | Call (f, xs) -> Call (f, List.map (subst args) xs)
answer.explain: Substitution only touches `Param` nodes, recurses structurally through `Add`, and at a nested `Call` rewrites the args but returns the body unchanged. That is the closed-body rule: the inner body's `Param 0` refers to the inner call's own args, so walking into it would wire in the wrong values.
